# Summary {.unnumbered}

We climbed the stack. Systems made a model dependable, applications turned
it into a product, and frontiers reached the questions still being
answered. At each step we asked the same thing: not only how the piece
works, but why it has the shape it does, what it gave up to get there, and
what foundation holds it up.

The layers depend on each other in both directions. A serving limit in
Part I becomes a latency budget for an agent in Part II. An evaluation
method from Part I becomes the only honest way to measure an autonomous
agent in Part III. A design that looks settled at one layer reopens as a
question at the next. Treating AI as an infrastructure means holding the
whole stack at once: the dashboard, the design history, and the equation
behind both.

## Where to go next

- Take one system you operate and write its history: the problem it solves,
  the design it settled on, what it superseded, and the trade-off it
  encodes.
- Read straight up the stack for one capability, from forward pass to
  autonomous agent, and watch where each layer's foundations carry up.
- Follow the Further reading at the end of each chapter to the primary
  sources behind every claim.
